solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: This place is finished!

parts.note: the clue names a seaside village whose name already ends in an exclamation mark, so the clue's own closing '!' completes the place-name

explanation.surface: An exasperated cry that some establishment is done for and closing down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Finished' looks like a verdict on a place that is ruined, but it means the exclamation mark itself completes the name. Westward Ho! is a village on the North Devon coast in England, named after a Charles Kingsley novel.
explanation.definitionFit: The Devon village is unusual in having an exclamation mark as part of its official name, which the clue supplies.

clue.text: Power unit, sorry to say

indicators.note: to say means the word is spoken, giving a sound-alike

parts.note: 'Sorry?' and 'What?' are both ways to ask someone to repeat themselves

explanation.surface: An apology about a power unit, delivered with regret.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sorry' looks like an apology but is the request 'Sorry?' when you have misheard.
explanation.definitionFit: The SI unit of power, one joule per second, named after James Watt.

clue.text: Spells 'dishy' phonetically?

indicators.note: phonetically means the word is written as it sounds, giving a sound-alike

parts.note: a made-up adjective, like a saucer; dishy is a jokey way to say saucer-like

explanation.surface: Someone spells out the word dishy as it sounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spells' looks like spelling words but is magic. 'dishy' (attractive) is taken as 'like a saucer'.
explanation.definitionFit: Magic charms and incantations, the practice of wizards, are spells collectively.

clue.text: Misanthrope running after wife most cheerfully

indicators.note: after means the scrambled word follows the letter for wife
running means the letters of misanthrope are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: A people-hater chases after his wife, in high spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'running' looks like the misanthrope jogging, but it signals the anagram; the hater ends up welcoming everyone, an ironic twist.
explanation.definitionFit: Welcoming someone warmly and eagerly, the idiom for a most cheerful reception.

clue.text: Transfer power when seizing a ship

indicators.note: seizing means the word for power grabs the following letters inside it

parts.note: to reign is to hold power; reign is rule
SS is the abbreviation for steamship

explanation.surface: Pirates hand over control as they capture a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: To move someone to a different post or task is to transfer them.

clue.text: Pilgrims enjoyed letter which starts 'Jesus lives'? Maybe

parts.note: had means enjoyed, as in had a good time

indicators.note: letter which starts means the opening letter of Jesus is taken

parts.note: is means exists or lives; the closing 'Maybe' admits the stretch

explanation.surface: Pilgrims enjoyed a letter opening with the words 'Jesus lives'.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'Maybe' signals that 'lives' only loosely means 'is' (exists).
explanation.definitionFit: Muslims who have made the pilgrimage to Mecca carry this title, so they are pilgrims.

clue.text: Crazy PM no good?

parts.note: PM means afternoon, not Prime Minister: if the afternoon is no good, the morning (AM) is OK, and those letters together mean crazy

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a deranged Prime Minister is any use.
explanation.walkthrough: PM reads as Prime Minister, but it is the afternoon. If an afternoon slot will not do, the morning is OK: AM + OK. 'Crazy' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Running wild or out of control is a frenzied state, close in sense to crazy.

clue.text: Tent damage — suspect base is missing

parts.note: to mar is to damage

indicators.note: in a down entry the base is the bottom, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: queer means suspect or dubious

explanation.surface: Damage to a tent is suspicious because its base has vanished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'base' looks like the tent's floor, but it is the last letter of the word in a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A large tent used for weddings, fairs and parties.

clue.text: Of modest design, in the area of caps

definitions.meaning: describes a skirt or dress of decent, not short, length
reaching to the kneecaps, the caps on the joints of the legs

explanation.surface: A fashion note on a sensible hemline reaching as far as the caps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'caps' looks like hats, but means the kneecaps.
explanation.definitionFit: A hemline down to the joint of the leg is modest, so not a mini, and sits around the kneecaps.

clue.text: They may predict return of player in some small ways

indicators.note: in places the turned player inside the word made from the small amount and the roads
some means only part of the word for a small amount is used, its last letter dropped

parts.note: a tad is a small amount
RDS is short for roads, which are ways

indicators.note: return of means the word for the player is read backwards

parts.note: an actor is a player on the stage

explanation.surface: A sportsman or performer comes back by various minor routes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return of' turns the player backwards; 'some' says only part of the word for small is used, and 'in' puts the turned player between that and the roads.
explanation.definitionFit: Fortune tellers lay out these picture cards to foretell the future, so they may predict what is to come.

clue.text: Wed after this, keeping Romeo faithful

indicators.note: keeping means the day abbreviation holds the next letter inside it

parts.note: Wednesday comes after Tuesday, abbreviated TUE
Romeo is R in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A wedding follows, and Romeo stays loyal to his bride.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wed' looks like getting married, but it is Wednesday; the day before it is Tuesday.
explanation.definitionFit: Being loyal and constant to someone is a direct synonym for faithful.

clue.text: Forged metals, mining being out?

indicators.note: forged means the letters of metals and mining are hammered into a new shape

explanation.surface: Metals are worked in a forge while the mining industry is on strike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being out' looks like going on strike, but here means not lined up.
explanation.definitionFit: The state of not being in line, such as wheels or teeth that are off true, is being out.

clue.text: Funny way to give the French king almost nothing

parts.note: a comic French accent pronounces 'the' as 'ze'

indicators.note: almost means the last letter of the French word is dropped

parts.note: roi is French for king

explanation.surface: Someone jokes about handing the King of France next to nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ze roi' is mock French for 'the king'; 'almost' drops its final I.
explanation.definitionFit: Nought, or nil, is the number for nothing at all.

clue.text: It's acceptable to break wind, and heavenly

indicators.note: to break means these letters split the word for wind into two parts

parts.note: to spiral is to wind or twist around
taken as written
U means upper-class, so socially acceptable

explanation.surface: A cheeky claim that passing wind is permitted, and even divine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wind' reads as flatulence but is the verb to coil, SPIRAL. U is the old label for upper-class, hence socially acceptable usage.
explanation.definitionFit: Something of the spirit or soul, concerned with religion, is heavenly rather than earthly.

clue.text: Win over British on home soil

parts.note: in means at home
ground is earth or soil

explanation.surface: A British victory achieved on home turf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Win over' reads like a victory, but it means persuade.
explanation.definitionFit: To persuade someone to your point of view is to win them over.

clue.text: Physicist developed early unlimited light

indicators.note: developed means the letters of early are worked into a new arrangement
unlimited means the word light loses its outer letters, keeping the inside

explanation.surface: A scientist made an early breakthrough with boundless light.
explanation.walkthrough: 'developed' rearranges EARLY into RAYLE; 'unlimited' strips light to IGH.
explanation.definitionFit: Lord Rayleigh was a British physicist and Nobel laureate who explained why the sky is blue.

clue.text: Gradually increase weird noise, say

indicators.note: say signals that the phrase is to be pronounced, giving a sound-alike

parts.note: fey means weird or otherworldly, and din is noise

explanation.surface: A sound engineer is told to slowly bring up a strange noise.
explanation.walkthrough: FEY DIN, said out loud, matches the film and sound term.
explanation.definitionFit: In film or audio, bringing a picture or sound up slowly from nothing is to increase it gradually.

clue.text: Virgin can, if taken by force

indicators.note: taken by means the word for can is held inside the word for force

parts.note: to prise is to force open with a lever
a tin is a can

explanation.surface: A tin can is forced open, as though seized by violence.
explanation.definitionFit: Unspoilt, untouched, in its original state, as virgin snow or a virgin forest.

clue.text: Awaiting confirmation in approval for fair

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation inside the word for approval

parts.note: a nod is a sign of approval
TBA, to be announced, marks something awaiting confirmation

explanation.surface: Plans for a fête still need final approval.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fair' looks like a fête, but it means middling, so-so.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something is reasonably good, middling but acceptable, is calling it fair.

clue.text: Temperature more strange around lake, little one

indicators.note: around means the stranger word goes round the letter for lake

parts.note: odder means more strange

explanation.surface: The temperature is behaving oddly near a lake, says a child.
explanation.definitionFit: A young child just learning to walk is a little one.

clue.text: Spooner's beast, plump flying fox

indicators.note: Spooner's signals that the opening sounds of two words are swapped

parts.note: a brute is a beast
fat means plump

explanation.surface: A description of a portly, airborne fox-like creature.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the opening sounds of BRUTE FAT gives FRUTE BAT, pronounced like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Flying foxes are large fruit-eating bats of the tropics, the commonest name for the creature.

clue.text: Evidence of poor hygiene? Smell from bottom (scientists)

parts.note: BO, body odour, is evidence of poor hygiene

indicators.note: from bottom means the word is read upwards in this down entry, so backwards

parts.note: to sniff is to smell

explanation.surface: A bad smell rising from someone's bottom shows poor hygiene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from bottom' looks lavatorial but means SNIFF reads upwards, giving FFINS.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for scientists or technical experts, especially those in research.

clue.text: Waiting for connection? Ring New Hampshire earlier

parts.note: a ring is round like the letter O
NH is the US state abbreviation for New Hampshire
old means of an earlier time

explanation.surface: Someone is told to phone New Hampshire sooner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring' looks like a phone call, but it gives O.
explanation.definitionFit: A caller kept waiting before being put through to the person they want is in that state.

clue.text: ABC… D,E… I'm poorly grasped by inferior kids

indicators.note: grasped by means the scrambled letters are held inside the word for the kids

parts.note: runts are the weakest, undersized young of a litter

indicators.note: poorly means the letters D, E, I and M are rearranged

parts.note: the letters D and E as printed
I'm gives the letters IM

explanation.surface: Struggling schoolchildren stumble over the alphabet, the narrator feeling unwell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poorly' rearranges D, E, I, M into DIME, held inside RUNTS. ABC… stands for the basics, the first things learnt.
explanation.definitionFit: Basic principles of a subject, like the alphabet in learning to read, are its first elements.

clue.text: Pathetic female admirer rejected

indicators.note: rejected means the words for female and admirer are turned back to front

parts.note: a fan is an admirer

explanation.surface: A sad woman with a crush is turned down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns F + FAN backwards. The answer is British slang for uncool or rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for tacky, lame or useless, close in sense to pathetic.

clue.text: Tax cut

definitions.meaning: a tax paid to the crown in Anglo-Saxon and medieval England
to castrate an animal, especially a horse

explanation.walkthrough: The tax was paid by landholders in medieval England. 'cut' means to castrate, as with a gelding.
explanation.definitionFit: One word means both a medieval royal levy and castrating an animal.

clue.text: Heads for unusual girl — extremely lively but not attractive

indicators.note: heads for means the first letters of the next two words are taken
extremely means the letters at both extremes of lively are taken

explanation.surface: An odd, very energetic girl who is not pretty.
explanation.definitionFit: Unpleasant to look at, the opposite of good-looking or appealing.

clue.text: Wooden bridges worried collie — do not cross!

indicators.note: bridges means the wooden word spans, so encloses, the scrambled dog

parts.note: pine is a wood, so wooden can mean made of pine

indicators.note: worried means the letters of collie are disturbed into a new order

explanation.surface: Timber footbridges have upset a sheepdog, so it is warned to stay off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wooden' is an adjective meaning made of pine; 'bridges' tells the wood to span the anagram, which 'worried' signals.
explanation.definitionFit: Tape stretched at a crime scene warns the public to stay out, which is the sense of do not cross.

clue.text: Daughter's chest hidden

parts.note: an ark is a chest or box, as in the Ark of the Covenant

explanation.surface: A girl's treasure box has been tucked away.
explanation.definitionFit: Kept secret or obscure, as in keeping something in the dark, means hidden.

clue.text: Plugged it in the wrong way opposing front of device

indicators.note: in places the turned letters inside the word for opposing

parts.note: adverse means opposing or hostile

indicators.note: the wrong way means the word it is read backwards
front of means the first letter of device is taken

explanation.surface: Someone wrongly plugged a gadget in, against the front of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plugged' reads like wiring up a plug, but means promoted. 'the wrong way' turns IT into TI.
explanation.definitionFit: To plug a product is to promote it publicly, the same as giving it publicity.
